title: Songs of the Ghost-Dance Religion (Mooney)
note: Songs of the Ghost Dance, as taken down by James Mooney and printed in The Ghost-Dance Religion and the Sioux Outbreak of 1890 (Fourteenth Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1896), Part II, 'The Songs', from Project Gutenberg no. 74335. Mooney's English renderings, numbered as the native texts. Comanche 2 and 4 are left out because Mooney gives no translation for them (he calls the first without meaning; the second is the Arapaho closing song, taken over by the Comanche). His notes on each song are left out.
blurb: Songs of the Ghost Dance of 1889-1891, sung by the Arapaho, Cheyenne, Comanche, Paiute, Lakota (Sioux), Kiowa and Caddo.
author: Anonymous (Plains nations)

sections.title: Arapaho 1. Eyehe′! nä′nisa′na.
sections.text:
O, my children! O, my children!
Here is another of your pipes—He′eye′!
Here is another of your pipes—He′eye′!
Look! thus I shouted—He′eye′!
Look! thus I shouted—He′eye′!
When I moved the earth—He′eye′!
When I moved the earth—He′eye′!

sections.title: Arapaho 2. Sĕ′icha hei′ta′wuni′na
sections.text:
The sacred pipe tells me—E′yahe′eye!
The sacred pipe tells me—E′yahe′eye!
Our father—Yahe′eye′!
Our father—Yahe′eye′!
We shall surely be put again (with our friends)—E′yahe′eye!
We shall surely be put again (with our friends)—E′yahe′eye!
Our father—E′yahe′eye!
Our father—E′yahe′eye!

sections.title: Arapaho 3. Ate′bĕ tiăwu′nănu′
sections.text:
My children, when at first I liked the whites,
My children, when at first I liked the whites,
I gave them fruits,
I gave them fruits.

sections.title: Arapaho 4. A′bä′ni′hi′
sections.text:
My partner, my partner,
Let us go out gambling,
Let us go out gambling,
At chi′chita′nĕ, at chi′chita′nĕ.

sections.title: Arapaho 5. A′-nisûna′a′hu Ächĭshinĭ′qahi′na
sections.text:
My father, my father,
While he was taking me around,
While he was taking me around,
He turned into a moose,
He turned into a moose.

sections.title: Arapaho 6. E′yehe′! Wû′nayu′uhu′
sections.text:
E′yehe′! they are new—
E′yehe′! they are new—
The bed coverings,
The bed coverings.

sections.title: Arapaho 7. Hi′sähi′hi
sections.text:
My partner! My partner!
Strike the ball hard—
Strike the ball hard.
I want to win,
I want to win.

sections.title: Arapaho 8. Ä′-nani′ni′bi′nä′si waku′na
sections.text:
My children, my children,
The wind makes the head-feathers sing—
The wind makes the head-feathers sing.
My children, my children.

sections.title: Arapaho 9. He′! Näne′th bi′shiqa′wă
sections.text:
He! When I met him approaching—
He! When I met him approaching—
My children, my children—
I then saw the multitude plainly,
I then saw the multitude plainly.

sections.title: Arapaho 10. Häna′na′wunănu ni′tawu′na′na′
sections.text:
My children, my children,
I take pity on those who have been taught,
I take pity on those who have been taught,
Because they push on hard,
Because they push on hard.
Says our father,
Says our father.

sections.title: Arapaho 11. A-ni′qu wa′wanä′nibä′tia′
sections.text:
Father, now I am singing it—Hi′ni′ni!
Father, now I am singing it—Hi′ni′ni!
That loudest song of all,
That loudest song of all—
That resounding song—Hi′ni′ni!
That resounding song—Hi′ni′ni!

sections.title: Arapaho 12. Ha′yana′-usi′ya′
sections.text:
How bright is the moonlight!
How bright is the moonlight!
Tonight as I ride with my load of buffalo beef,
Tonight as I ride with my load of buffalo beef.

sections.title: Arapaho 13. Ha′ti ni′bät—E′he′eye′
sections.text:
The cottonwood song—E′he′eye′!
The cottonwood song—E′he′eye′!
I am singing it,
I am singing it,
He′yäya′ahe′ye!
He′yäya′ahe′ye!

sections.title: Arapaho 14. Eyehe′! A′nie′sa′na
sections.text:
Eyehe′! The young birds,
Eyehe′! The young birds,
He′ee′ä′ehe′yuhe′yu!
He′ee′ä′ehe′yuhe′yu!
The young Thunderbirds,
The young Thunderbirds.

sections.title: Arapaho 15. A′he′sûna′nini năya′qûti′hi
sections.text:
Our father, the Whirlwind,
Our father, the Whirlwind—
By its aid I am running swiftly,
By its aid I am running swiftly,
By which means I saw our father,
By which means I saw our father.

sections.title: Arapaho 16. A′he′sûna′nini năya′qûti′
sections.text:
Our father, the Whirlwind,
Our father, the Whirlwind,
Now wears the headdress of crow feathers,
Now wears the headdress of crow feathers.

sections.title: Arapaho 17. Ninaä′niahu′na
sections.text:
I circle around—
I circle around
The boundaries of the earth,
The boundaries of the earth—
Wearing the long wing feathers as I fly,
Wearing the long wing feathers as I fly.

sections.title: Arapaho 18. Ha′nahawu′nĕn bĕni′ni′na
sections.text:
The Hanahawunĕn gave to me,
The Hanahawunĕn gave to me,
His paint—He made me clean,
His paint—He made me clean.

sections.title: Arapaho 19. Ate′be′tana′-ise′ti he′sûna′nini′
sections.text:
When first our father came—Ahe′eye′!
When first our father came—Ahe′eye′!
I prayed to him, I prayed to him—
My relative, my relative—
He′yahe′eỹe′!

sections.title: Arapaho 20. A-ni′änĕ′thăhi′nani′na nisa′na
sections.text:
My father did not recognize me (at first),
My father did not recognize me (at first).
When again he saw me,
When again he saw me,
He said, “You are the offspring of a crow,”
He said, “You are the offspring of a crow.”

sections.title: Arapaho 21. Ni′-athu′-a-u′ a′hakä′nith′iĭ
sections.text:
I′yehe′! my children—Uhi′yeye′heye′!
I′yehe′! my children—Uhi′yeye′heye′!
I′yehe′! we have rendered them desolate—Eye′ăe′yuhe′yu!
I′yehe′! we have rendered them desolate—Eye′ăe′yuhe′yu!
The whites are crazy—Ahe′yuhe′yu!

sections.title: Arapaho 22. Na′ha′ta bitaa′wu
sections.text:
My children, my children,
Look! the earth is about to move,
Look! the earth is about to move.
My father tells me so,
My father tells me so.

sections.title: Arapaho 23. Ahe′sûna′nini Ächiqa′hă′wa-ü′
sections.text:
My father, my father—
I am looking at him,
I am looking at him.
He is beginning to turn into a bird,
He is beginning to turn into a bird.

sections.title: Arapaho 24. Ha′ănake′i
sections.text:
The rock, the rock,
I am standing upon it,
I am standing upon it.
By its means I saw our father,
By its means I saw our father.

sections.title: Arapaho 25. Wa′wa′na′danä′diă′
sections.text:
My children, my children,
I am about to hum,
I am about to hum.
My children, my children.

sections.title: Arapaho 26. A-te′bĕ′ dii′nĕtita′niĕg
sections.text:
At the beginning of human existence—I′yehe′eye′!
At the beginning of human existence—I′yehe′eye′!
It was the turtle who gave this grateful gift to me—
The earth—I′yehe′eye′!
It was the turtle who gave this grateful gift to me—
The earth—I′yehe′eye′!
(Thus) my father told me—Ahe′eye′-he′eye′!
(Thus) my father told me—Ahe′eye′-he′eye′!

sections.title: Arapaho 27. Tahu′na′änä′nia′huna
sections.text:
My children, my children,
It is I who make the thunder as I circle about—
The thunder as I circle about.
My children, my children,
It is I who make the loud thunder as I circle about—
The loud thunder as I circle about.

sections.title: Arapaho 28. Ani′qu ne′chawu′nani′
Arapaho 29. A-ni′niha′niahu′na
sections.text:
I fly around yellow,
I fly around yellow,
I fly with the wild rose on my head,
I fly with the wild rose on my head,
On high—He′e′e′!
On high—He′e′e′!

sections.title: Arapaho 30. Niha′nata′yeche′ti
sections.text:
The yellow-hide, the white-skin (man).
I have now put him aside—
I have now put him aside—
I have no more sympathy with him,
I have no more sympathy with him.
He′yoho′ho′! He′yoho′ho′!

sections.title: Arapaho 31. A-bää′thina′hu
sections.text:
The cedar tree, the cedar tree,
We have it in the center,
We have it in the center
When we dance,
When we dance.
We have it in the center,
We have it in the center.

sections.title: Arapaho 32. Wa′wa nû′nanû′naku′ti
sections.text:
My children, my children,
Now I am waving an eagle feather,
Now I am waving an eagle feather.
Here is a spotted feather for you,
Here is a spotted feather for you.
You may have it, said my father,
You may have it, said my father.

sections.title: Arapaho 33. A-ni′qana′ga
sections.text:
There is a solitary bull,
There is a solitary bull—
I am going to use him to “make medicine,”
I am going to use him to “make medicine.”

sections.title: Arapaho 34. A-nĕä′thibiwă′hană
sections.text:
The place where crying begins,
The place where crying begins—
The thi′äya,
The thi′äya.

sections.title: Arapaho 35. Thi′äya he′năă′awă′
sections.text:
When I see the thi′äya—
When I see the thi′äya,
Then I begin to lament,
Then I begin to lament.

sections.title: Arapaho 36. A-hu′hu ha′geni′sti′ti ba′hu
sections.text:
The crow is making a road,
He is making a road.
He has finished it,
He has finished it.
His children,
His children—
Then he collected them,
Then he collected them (i. e., on the farther side).

sections.title: Arapaho 37. Bi′taa′wu hu′hu′
sections.text:
The earth—the crow,
The earth—the crow—
The crow brought it with him,
The crow brought it with him—
A′hene′heni′ă′ă′! A′he′yene′hene′!

sections.title: Arapaho 38. Ni′nini′tubi′na hu′hu′—I
sections.text:
The crow has called me,
The crow has called me.
When the crow came for me,
When the crow came for me,
I heard him,
I heard him.

sections.title: Arapaho 39. Nû′nanû′naa′tăni′na hu′hu′—I
sections.text:
The crow is circling above me,
The crow is circling above me,
The crow having come for me,
The crow having come for me.

sections.title: Arapaho 40. I′yu hä′thäbĕ′nawa′
sections.text:
My children—E′e′ye′!
My children—E′e′ye′!
Here it is, I hand it to you.
The earth—E′e′ye′!
The earth—E′e′ye′!

sections.title: Arapaho 41. Ha′naĕ′hi ya′ga′ahi′na
sections.text:
Little boy, the coyote gun—
Little boy, the coyote gun—
I have uncovered it—Ahe′e′ye′!
I have uncovered it—Ahe′e′ye′!
There is the sheath lying there,
There is the sheath lying there.

sections.title: Arapaho 42. He′sûna′ na′nahatha′hi
sections.text:
The father showed me,
The father showed me.
Where they were coming down,
Where they were coming down.

sections.title: Arapaho 43. Nänisa′tăqu′thi Chĭnachi′chibä′iha′
sections.text:
The seven venerable Chĭ′nachichi′bät priests,
The seven venerable Chĭ′nachichi′bät priests—
We see them,
We see them.
They all wear it on their heads—
They all wear it on their heads—
The Thunderbird,
The Thunderbird.
Then I wept,
Then I wept.

sections.title: Arapaho 44. Nänisa′tăqi Chĭ′năchi′chibä′iha′
sections.text:
The seven venerable Chĭnachichi′bät priests—
The seven venerable Chĭnachichi′bät priests—
For them I am weeping,
For them I am weeping.
For the gaming wheel I am weeping,
For the gaming wheel I am weeping.

sections.title: Arapaho 45. Nû′nanû′naatani′na hu′hu′—II
sections.text:
The crow is circling above me,
The crow is circling above me.
He says he will give me a hawk feather,
He says he will give me a hawk feather.

sections.title: Arapaho 46. Na′tănu′ya chĕ′bi′nh
sections.text:
The pemmican that I am using—
The pemmican that I am using,
They are still making it,
They are still making it.

sections.title: Arapaho 47. Häĭ′nawa′ hä′ni′ta′quna′ni
sections.text:
I know, in the pitfall—
I know, in the pitfall—
It is tallow they use in the pitfall,
It is tallow they use in the pitfall.

sections.title: Arapaho 48. Bä′hinä′nina′tä ni′tabä′na
sections.text:
I hear everything,
I hear everything.
I am the crow,
I am the crow.

sections.title: Arapaho 49. A-bä′qati′ hä′nichä′bi′hinä′na
sections.text:
With the bä′qati wheel I am gambling,
With the bä′qati wheel I am gambling.
With the black mark I win the game,
With the black mark I win the game.

sections.title: Arapaho 50. Ani′äsa′kua′na dă′chäbi′hati′tani
sections.text:
I am watching where they are gambling with the bä′qati wheel,
I am watching where they are gambling with the bä′qati wheel.
They are rolling the bä′qati,
They are rolling the bä′qati.
While they gamble with it,
While they gamble with it.

sections.title: Arapaho 51. Ni′chi′a i′theti′hi
sections.text:
(There) is a good river,
(There) is a good river,
Where there is no timber—
Where there is no timber—
But thunder-berries are there,
But thunder-berries are there.

sections.title: Arapaho 52. Ni′nini′tubi′na hu′hu′
sections.text:
The crow has given me the signal,
The crow has given me the signal.
When the crow makes me dance,
When the crow makes me dance,
He tells me (when) to stop,
He tells me (when) to stop.

sections.title: Arapaho 53. Anihä′ya atani′tă′nu′nawa′
sections.text:
I use the yellow (paint),
I use the yellow (paint),
Says the father,
Says the father,
In order to please me, the father,
In order to please me, the father—Ih! Ih!

sections.title: Arapaho 54. Ni′naä′niahu′tawa bi′taa′wu
sections.text:
My children, my children,
I am flying about the earth,
I am flying about the earth.
I am a bird, my children,
I am a bird, my children,
Says the father,
Says the father.

sections.title: Arapaho 55. I′nita′ta′-usä′na
sections.text:
Stand ready,
Stand ready.
(So that when) the crow calls you,
(So that when) the crow calls you.
You will see him,
You will see him.

sections.title: Arapaho 56. Wa′wäthä′bi
sections.text:
My children, my children,
I have given you magpie feathers again to wear on your heads—He′e′ye′!
Thus says our mother,
Thus says our mother.

sections.title: Arapaho 57. Ani′qa hĕ′tabi′nuhu′ni′na
sections.text:
My father, I am poor,
My father, I am poor.
Our father is about to take pity on me,
Our father is about to take pity on me.
Our father is about to make me fly around.
Our father is about to make me fly around.

sections.title: Arapaho 58. Nä′nisa′taqu′thi hu′na
sections.text:
The seven crows—Hi′ă hi′ni′ni′!
The seven crows—Hi′ă hi′ni′ni′!
They are flying about the carrion—Hi′ă hi′ni′ni′!
They are flying about the carrion—Hi′ă hi′ni′ni′!

sections.title: Arapaho 59. Ahu′nä he′sûna′nĭn
sections.text:
There is our father—
There is our father—
We are dancing as he wishes (makes) us to dance,
We are dancing as he wishes (makes) us to dance,
Because our father has so commanded us,
Because our father has so commanded us.

sections.title: Arapaho 60. Ga′awa′hu
sections.text:
The ball, the ball—
You must throw it swiftly,
You must throw it swiftly.
I want to win,
I want to win.

sections.title: Arapaho 61. Ahu′ ni′higa′hu
sections.text:
The Crow is running,
The Crow is running.
He will hear me.
He will hear me.

sections.title: Arapaho 62. Ya′thä-yû′na ta′na-u′qahe′na
sections.text:
My father—He′e′ye′!
My father—He′e′ye′!
He put me in five places—He′e′ye′!
He put me in five places—He′e′ye′!
I stood upon the earth—He′e′ye′!
I stood upon the earth—He′e′ye′!

sections.title: Arapaho 63. Ni′naäqa′wa chibä′ti
sections.text:
I am going around the sweat-house,
I am going around the sweat-house.
The shell lies upon the mound,
The shell lies upon the mound.

sections.title: Arapaho 64. Hise′hi, hise′hi
sections.text:
My comrade, my comrade,
Let us play the awl game,
Let us play the awl game,
Let us play the dice game,
Let us play the dice game.

sections.title: Arapaho 65. Na′tu′wani′sa
sections.text:
My children, my children,
My top, my top—
It will win the game,
It will win the game.

sections.title: Arapaho 66. He′na′ga′nawa′nen
sections.text:
When we dance until daylight our father, the Moon, takes pity on
us—Ahe′e′ye′!
When we dance until daylight our father, the Moon, takes pity on
us—Ahe′e′ye′!
The father says so—Ahe′e′ye′!
The father says so—Ahe′e′ye′!

sections.title: Arapaho 67. Ni′nä′nina′ti′naku′ni′na na′ga′qu′
sections.text:
My children, my children,
It is I who wear the morning star on my head.
It is I who wear the morning star on my head;
I show it to my children,
I show it to my children,
Says the father,
Says the father.

sections.title: Arapaho 68. A′-nena′ tabi′ni′na
sections.text:
My mother gave me my tĭ′qtawa stick,
My mother gave me my tĭ′qtawa stick.
I fly around with it,
I fly around with it,
To make me see my children,
To make me see my children.

sections.title: Arapaho 69. Yĭ′hä′ä′ä′hi′hĭ′
sections.text:
Yĭ′hä′ä′ä′hi′hĭ′, Yĭ′hä′ä′ä′hi′hĭ′,
I throw the “button,”
I throw the “button.”

sections.title: Arapaho 70. Ni′qa-hu′hu′
sections.text:
My father, my father,
I go straight to it, I go straight to it—
The ga′qaä, the ga′qaä.

sections.title: Arapaho 71. A′hu′nawu′hu′
sections.text:
With red paint, with red paint,
I want to paint myself—He′e′ye′!
I want to paint myself—He′e′ye′!
When I play ga′qutit,
When I play ga′qutit.
It is the “button”—He′e′ye′!
It is the “button”—He′e′ye′!

sections.title: Arapaho 72. Ani′qa naga′qu
sections.text:
Father, the Morning Star!
Father, the Morning Star!
Look on us, we have danced until daylight,
Look on us, we have danced until daylight.
Take pity on us—Hi′i′i′!
Take pity on us—Hi′i′i′!

sections.title: Arapaho 73. Ahu′yu häthi′na
sections.text:
Thus says our father, the Crow,
Thus says our father, the Crow.
Go around five times more—
Go around five times more—
Says the father,
Says the father.

sections.title: Cheyenne 1. O′tä nä′nisĭ′näsists
sections.text:
Well, my children—Ehe′e′ye′!
Well, my children—Ehe′e′ye′!
When you meet your friends again—Ähe′e′ye′!
When you meet your friends again—Ähe′e′ye′!
The earth will tremble—E′ähe′e′ye′!
The earth will tremble—E′ähe′e′ye′!
The summer cloud (?)
It will give it to us,
It will give it to us.

sections.title: Cheyenne 2. Ehä′n esho′ini′
sections.text:
Our father has come,
Our father has come,
The earth has come,
The earth has come,
It is rising—Eye′ye′!
It is rising—Eye′ye′!
It is humming—Ahe′e′ye′!
It is humming—Ahe′e′ye′!

sections.title: Cheyenne 3. Nä′niso′näsĭ′stsihi′
sections.text:
My children, my children,
Here is the river of turtles,
Here is the river of turtles,
Where the various living things,
Where the various living things,
Are painted their different colors,
Are painted their different colors.
Our father says so,
Our father says so.

sections.title: Cheyenne 4. Nä′see′nehe′ ehe′yowo′mi
sections.text:
I waded into the yellow river,
I waded into the yellow river,
This was the Turtle river into which I waded,
This was the Turtle river into which I waded.

sections.title: Cheyenne 5. Wosi′vä-ă′ă′
sections.text:
The mountain,
The mountain,
It is circling around,
It is circling around,
Ä′hiya′e′yee′heye′!
Ä′hiya′e′yee′heye′!

sections.title: Cheyenne 6. Ni′ha-i′hi′hi′
sections.text:
My father,
My father,
I come to him,
I come to him,
The crow,
The crow,
I cry like it,
I cry like it,
Caw! I say,
Caw! I say.

sections.title: Cheyenne 7. Hi′awu′hi—hi′hi′hai′-yai′
sections.text:
The devil—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
The devil—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
We have put him aside—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
We have put him aside—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
The White Man Above—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
The White Man Above—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
He is our father—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
He is our father—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
He has blest us—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!
He has blest us—Hi′hi′hai′-yai′!

sections.title: Cheyenne 8. Ni′ha—E′yehe′! E′he′eye
sections.text:
My father—E′yehe′! E′he′eye′!
My father—E′yehe′! E′he′eye′!
When I first met him—Ehe′eye′!
When I first met him—Ehe′eye′!
“In the blue-green water—He′eye′!”
”In the blue-green-water—He′eye′!”
“You must take a bath“—He′eye′!”
“You must take a bath”—He′eye′!”
Thus he told me, thus he told me—He′!

sections.title: Cheyenne 9. Ä′minû′qi
sections.text:
My comrade—I′yahe′yahe′e′!
My comrade—I′yahe′yahe′e′!
Let us go and play shinny—Ahe′e′ye′!
Let us go and play shinny—Ahe′e′ye′!
Let us look for our mother—Ahe′e′ye′!
Let us look for our mother—Ahe′e′ye′!
Our father tells us to do it—Ahe′e′ye′!
Our father tells us to do it—Ahe′e′ye′!

sections.title: Cheyenne 10. He′stutu′ai
sections.text:
The buffalo head—Yä′hä′yä′!
The half buffalo—
[Ad libitum].

sections.title: Cheyenne 11. Nä′mio′ts
sections.text:
I am coming in sight—Ehe′ee′ye′!
I am coming in sight—Ehe′ee′ye′!
I bring the whirlwind with me—E′yahe′eye′!
I bring the whirlwind with me—E′yahe′eye′!
That you may see each other—
That you may see each other.

sections.title: Cheyenne 12. A′gachi′hi
sections.text:
The crow, the crow,
He is circling around,
He is circling around,
His wing, his wing—
I am dancing with it,
I am dancing with it.

sections.title: Cheyenne 13. Nä′nise′näsĕ′stse
sections.text:
My children, I am now humming—He′eye′!
My children, I am now humming—He′eye′!
Your children, your children,
They are crying—He′eye′!
They are crying—He′eye′!
They are hurrying me along,
They are hurrying me along.

sections.title: Cheyenne 14. Ogo′ch—Ehe′eye′
sections.text:
The crow—Ehe′eye′!
The crow—Ehe′eye′!
I saw him when he flew down,
I saw him when he flew down.
To the earth, to the earth.
He has renewed our life,
He has renewed our life.
He has taken pity on us,
He has taken pity on us.

sections.title: Cheyenne 15. Tsĭso′soyo′tsĭto′ho
sections.text:
While I was going about,
While I was going about,
Among the people, at my home,
Among the people, at my home,
I saw them,
I saw them,
Where they gambled,
Where they gambled,
With the ä‛ko′yo wheel,
With the ä‛ko′yo wheel.

sections.title: Cheyenne 16. Ni′ha—E′yehe′e′yeye′
sections.text:
My father—E′yehe′e′yeye′!
My father—E′yehe′e′yeye′!
His children—Hi′yeye′!
His children—Hi′yeye′!
In the greenish water—He′e′ye′!
In the greenish water—He′e′ye′!
He makes them swim—He′eye′!
He makes them swim—He′eye′!
We are all crying—Ähe′eye′!
We are all crying—Ähe′eye′!

sections.title: Cheyenne 17. A′ga′ch—Ehe′e′ye′
sections.text:
The crow—Ehe′e′ye′!
The crow—Ehe′e′ye′!
The grease paint—He′e′ye′!
The grease paint—He′e′ye′!
He brings it to me,
He brings it to me.
The red paint—He′e′ye′!
The red paint—He′e′ye′!
He brings it,
He brings it.
I prepare myself with it,
I prepare myself with it.
It will make you strong,
It will make you strong.
He tells me, He tells me.

sections.title: Cheyenne 18. Nä′niso′näsĭ′stsi—He′e′ye′
sections.text:
My children—He′e′ye′!
My children—He′e′ye′!

Kill a buffalo (or beef) for the Crow—Ahe′e′ye′!
Kill a buffalo (or beef) for the Crow—Ahe′e′ye′!
By that means I shall see you,
By that means I shall see you.

sections.title: Cheyenne 19. A′guga′-ihi
sections.text:
The crow woman—
The crow woman—
To her home,
To her home,
She is going,
She is going.
She will see it,
She will see it.
Her children,
Her children.
She will see them,
She will see them.

sections.title: Comanche 1. Heyo′hänä Häe′yo
sections.text:
He′e′yo′!
Heyo′hänä′ Häe′yo!
Heyo′hänä′ Häe′yo!
The sun’s beams are running out—He′e′yo′!
The sun’s beams are running out—He′e′yo′!
The sun’s yellow rays are running out—Ähi′ni′yo′!
The sun’s yellow rays are running out—Ähi′ni′yo′!

sections.title: Comanche 3. Yani′tsini′hawa′na
sections.text:
Yani′tsini′hawa′na!
Yani′tsini′hawa′na!
We shall live again,
We shall live again.

sections.title: Paiute 1. Nüvä′ ka ro′răni′
sections.text:
The snow lies there—ro′răni′!
The snow lies there—ro′răni′!
The snow lies there—ro′răni′!
The snow lies there—ro′răni′!
The Milky Way lies there,
The Milky Way lies there.

sections.title: Paiute 2. Dĕna′ gayo′n
sections.text:
A slender antelope, a slender antelope,
A slender antelope, a slender antelope,
He is wallowing upon the ground,
He is wallowing upon the ground,
He is wallowing upon the ground,
He is wallowing upon the ground.

sections.title: Paiute 3. Do′ tĭ′mbi
sections.text:
The black rock, the black rock,
The black rock, the black rock,
The rock is broken, the rock is broken,
The rock is broken, the rock is broken.

sections.title: Paiute 4. Päsü′ wĭ′noghän
sections.text:
The wind stirs the willows,
The wind stirs the willows,
The wind stirs the willows,
The wind stirs the grasses,
The wind stirs the grasses,
The wind stirs the grasses.

sections.title: Paiute 5. Pägü′nävä′
sections.text:
Fog! Fog!
Lightning! Lightning!
Whirlwind! Whirlwind!

sections.title: Paiute 6. Wûmbĭ′ndomä′n
sections.text:
The whirlwind! The whirlwind!
The whirlwind! The whirlwind!
The snowy earth comes gliding, the snowy earth comes gliding;
The snowy earth comes gliding, the snowy earth comes gliding.

sections.title: Paiute 7. Kosi′ wûmbi′ndomä′
sections.text:
There is dust from the whirlwind,
There is dust from the whirlwind,
There is dust from the whirlwind.
The whirlwind on the mountain,
The whirlwind on the mountain,
The whirlwind on the mountain.

sections.title: Paiute 8. Dombi′na so′wina′
sections.text:
The rocks are ringing,
The rocks are ringing,
The rocks are ringing.
They are ringing in the mountains,
They are ringing in the mountains,
They are ringing in the mountains.

sections.title: Paiute 9. Sû′ng-ä ro′yonji′
sections.text:
The cottonwoods are growing tall,
The cottonwoods are growing tall,
The cottonwoods are growing tall.
They are growing tall and verdant,
They are growing tall and verdant,
They are growing tall and verdant.

sections.title: Sioux 1. A′te he′ye e′yayo
sections.text:
The father says so—E′yayo!
The father says so—E′yayo!
The father says so,
The father says so.
You shall see your grandfather—E′yayo′!
You shall see your grandfather—E′yayo′!
The father says so,
The father says so.
You shall see your kindred—E′yayo′!
You shall see your kindred—E′yayo′!
The father says so,
The father says so.

sections.title: Sioux 2. Mi′chĭ′nkshi nañpe
sections.text:
My son, let me grasp your hand,
My son, let me grasp your hand,
Says the father,
Says the father.
You shall live,
You shall live,
Says the father,
Says the father.
I bring you a pipe,
I bring you a pipe,
Says the father,
Says the father.
By means of it you shall live,
By means of it you shall live,
Says the father,
Says the father.

sections.title: Sioux 3. He tuwe′cha he
sections.text:
Who think you comes there?
Who think you comes there?
Is it someone looking for his mother?
Is it someone looking for his mother?
Says the father,
Says the father.

sections.title: Sioux 4. Wana′yañ ma′niye
sections.text:
Now he is walking,
Now he is walking.
There is a buffalo bull walking,
There is a buffalo bull walking,
Says the father,
Says the father.

sections.title: Sioux 5. Lechel miyo′qañ-kte
sections.text:
This is to be my work—Yo′yoyo′!
This is to be my work—Yo′yoyo′!
All that grows upon the earth is mine—Yo′yoyo′!
All that grows upon the earth is mine—Yo′yoyo′!
Says the father—Yo′yoyo′!
Says the father—Yo′yoyo′!
E′ya Yo′yoyo′!
E′ya Yo′yoyo′!

sections.title: Sioux 6. Michinkshi′yi tewa′qila che
sections.text:
I love my children—Ye′ye′!
I love my children—Ye′ye′!
You shall grow to be a nation—Ye′ye′!
You shall grow to be a nation—Ye′ye′!
Says the father, says the father.
Haye′ye′ E′yayo′yo′! Haye′ye′ E′yayo′yo′!

sections.title: Sioux 7. Mila kiñ hiyu′michi′chiyana
sections.text:
Give me my knife,
Give me my knife,
I shall hang up the meat to dry—Ye′ye′!
I shall hang up the meat to dry—Ye′ye′!
Says grandmother—Yo′yo′!
Says grandmother—Yo′yo′!
When it is dry I shall make pemmican,
When it is dry I shall make pemmican,
Says grandmother—Yo′yo!
Says grandmother—Yo′yo!

sections.title: Sioux 8. Le he′yahe′
sections.text:
This one says—Ye′ye!
This one says—Ye′ye!
I belong indeed to the nation of Crows,
I belong indeed to the nation of Crows.

sections.title: Sioux 9. Niya′te-ye′ he′uw′e
sections.text:
It is your father coming, it is your father coming,
A spotted eagle is coming for you,
A spotted eagle is coming for you.

sections.title: Sioux 10. Miyo′qañ kiñ wañla′ki
sections.text:
You see what I can do—Ye′yeye′!
You see what I can do—Ye′yeye′!
You see them, you see them,
Ha′eye′ya he′yeye′! Ha′eye′ya he′yeye′!

sections.title: Sioux 11. Michĭ′nkshi mita′waye
sections.text:
It is my own child,
It is my own child.

sections.title: Sioux 12. A′te he′ u-we
sections.text:
There is the father coming,
There is the father coming.
The father says this as he comes,
The father says this as he comes,
“You shall live,” he says as he comes,
“You shall live,” he says as he comes.

sections.title: Sioux 13. Wa′sna wa′tiñ-kta′
sections.text:
I shall eat pemmican—E′yeye′yeye′!
I shall eat pemmican—E′yeye′yeye′!
They say so, they say so,
The father says so, the father says so.

sections.title: Sioux 14. A′te lena ma′qu-we
sections.text:
It was the father who gave us these things—Ye′ye′ye′!
It was the father who gave us these things—Ye′ye′ye′!
It was the father who gave us fire—Ye′ye′ye′!
It was the father who gave us fire—Ye′ye′ye′!
The father gave it to us—Ye′ye′ye′!
The father gave it to us—Ye′ye′ye′!

sections.title: Sioux 15. Ina′ he′kuwo′
sections.text:
Mother, come home; mother, come home.
My little brother goes about always crying,
My little brother goes about always crying.
Mother, come home; mother, come home.

sections.title: Sioux 16. Wa′na wanasa′pi-kta
sections.text:
Now they are about to chase the buffalo,
Now they are about to chase the buffalo,
Grandmother, give me back my bow,
Grandmother, give me back my bow,
The father says so, the father says so.

sections.title: Sioux 17. He′! kii′ñyañka a′gali′-ye
sections.text:
He! They have come back racing,
He! They have come back racing,
Why, they say there is to be a buffalo hunt over here,
Why, they say there is to be a buffalo hunt over here,
Make arrows! Make arrows!
Says the father, says the father.

sections.title: Sioux 18. Mi′ye wañma′yañka-yo
sections.text:
Look at me! Look at me!
I make a road for one of the Crow nation (?),
I make a road for one of the Crow nation (?).
You shall live indeed, you shall live indeed.
Our friend says so, our friend says so.

sections.title: Sioux 19. Maka′ sito′maniyañ
sections.text:
The whole world is coming,
A nation is coming, a nation is coming,
The Eagle has brought the message to the tribe.
The father says so, the father says so.
Over the whole earth they are coming.
The buffalo are coming, the buffalo are coming,
The Crow has brought the message to the tribe,
The father says so, the father says so.

sections.title: Sioux 20. Le′na wa′kañ
sections.text:
It is I who make these sacred things,
Says the father, says the father.
It is I who make the sacred shirt,
Says the father, says the father.
It is I who made the pipe,
Says the father, says the father.

sections.title: Sioux 21. Miyo′qañ kiñ chichu′-che
sections.text:
Verily, I have given you my strength,
Says the father, says the father.
The shirt will cause you to live,
Says the father, says the father.

sections.title: Sioux 22. Michĭ′nkshi tahe′na
sections.text:
My child, come this way,
My child, come this way.
You will take home with you a good country,
Says the father, says the father.

sections.title: Sioux 23. Wana wichĕ′shka
sections.text:
Now set up the tipi,
Now set up the tipi.
Around the bottom,
Around the bottom,
Drive in the pegs,
Drive in the pegs.
In the meantime I shall cook,
In the meantime I shall cook.

sections.title: Sioux 24. A′te mi′chuye
sections.text:
Father, give them to me,
Father, give them to me,
Give me my arrows,
Give me my arrows.
They have come, they have come.
I shall eat pemmican,
I shall eat pemmican.

sections.title: Sioux 25. Hañpa wecha′ghe
sections.text:
I made moccasins for him,
I made moccasins for him,
For I love him,
For I love him.
To take to the orphan,
To take to the orphan.

Soon I shall see my child,
Soon I shall see my child,
Says your mother,
Says your mother.

sections.title: Sioux 26. Waka′ñyañ iñya′ñkiñ-kte
sections.text:
The holy (hoop) shall run,
The holy (hoop) shall run,
The swift hoop shall run,
The swift hoop shall run.
Come and see it,
Come and see it,
Says the father,
Says the father.

sections.title: Kiowa 1. Da′ta-i so′da′te
sections.text:
The father will descend,
The father will descend.
The earth will tremble,
The earth will tremble.
Everybody will arise,
Everybody will arise.
Stretch out your hands,
Stretch out your hands.

sections.title: Kiowa 2. Da′k̔′ñago (ĭm) zä′nteähe′dal
sections.text:
The spirit army is approaching,
The spirit army is approaching,
The whole world is moving onward,
The whole world is moving onward.
See! Everybody is standing watching,
See! Everybody is standing watching.
Let us all pray,
Let us all pray.

sections.title: Kiowa 3. Gu′ato ädâ′ga
sections.text:
I scream because I am a bird,
I scream because I am a bird,
I bellow like a buffalo,
I bellow like a buffalo.
The boy will rise up,
The boy will rise up.

sections.title: Kiowa 4. Da′ta-i nyä′hoănga′mo
sections.text:
Ä′häyä′ Ehä′eho′! Ä′häyä′ Ehä′eho′!
E′häyä′ Ehä′eho′! E′häyä′ Ehä′eho′!
The father shows me the road,
The father shows me the road.
I went to see my friends,
I went to see my friends,
I went to see the dances,
I went to see the dances.

sections.title: Kiowa 5. Dak̔iñ′a bate′yä
sections.text:
The spirit (God) is approaching,
The spirit (God) is approaching.
He is going to give me a bird tail,
He is going to give me a bird tail.
He will give it to me in the tops of the cottonwoods,
He will give it to me in the tops of the cottonwoods.

sections.title: Kiowa 6. Na′da′g äka′na
sections.text:
Heyĕ′heyĕ′heyĕ′heye′ Äho′ho′!
Heyĕ′heyĕ′heyĕ′heye′ Äho′ho′!
Because I am poor,
Because I am poor,
I pray for every living creature,
I pray for every living creature.
Äo′ñyo! Äo′ñyo!

sections.title: Kiowa 7. Ze′bät-gâ′ga igu′ănpa′-ima′
sections.text:
He makes me dance with arrows,
He makes me dance with arrows.
He calls the bow my father,

He calls the bow my father.
Grandmother, persevere,
Grandmother, persevere.

sections.title: Kiowa 8. Be′ta! To′ngyä-gu′adăl
sections.text:
Now I understand! Red Tail has been sent,
Now I understand! Red Tail has been sent.
We cry and hold fast to him,
We cry and hold fast to him.
He was made to live a long time,
He was made to live a long time.

sections.title: Kiowa 9. Da′ta′-i änka′ñgo′na
sections.text:
My father has much pity for us,
My father has much pity for us.
I hold out my hands toward him and cry,
I hold out my hands toward him and cry.
In my poverty I hold out my hands toward him and cry,
In my poverty I hold out my hands toward him and cry.

sections.title: Kiowa 10. Da′ta-i iñka′ñtähe′dal
sections.text:
Ähä′yä Ehä′eho′,
Ähä′yä Ehä′eho′.
My father has had pity on me.
I have eyes like my father’s,
I have hands like my father’s,
I have legs like my father’s,
I have a form like my father’s.

sections.title: Kiowa 11. Dak`iñ′ago äho′ähe′dal
sections.text:
The spirit host is advancing, they say,
The spirit host is advancing, they say.
They are coming with the buffalo, they say,
They are coming with the buffalo, they say.
They are coming with the (new) earth, they say,
They are coming with the (new) earth, they say.

sections.title: Kiowa 12. E′hyu′ñi degi′ăta
sections.text:
I am mashing the berries,
I am mashing the berries.
They say travelers are coming on the march,
They say travelers are coming on the march.
I stir (the berries) around, I stir them around;
I take them up with a spoon of buffalo horn,
I take them up with a spoon of buffalo horn,
And I carry them, I carry them (to the strangers),
And I carry them, I carry them (to the strangers).

sections.title: Kiowa 13. Go′mgyä-da′ga
sections.text:
That wind, that wind
Shakes my tipi, shakes my tipi,
And sings a song for me,
And sings a song for me.

sections.title: Kiowa 14. Dak̔iñ′a daka′ñtähe′dal
sections.text:
God has had pity on us,
God has had pity on us.
Jesus has taken pity on us,
Jesus has taken pity on us.
He teaches me a song,
He teaches me a song.
My song is a good one,
My song is a good one.

sections.title: Kiowa 15. Anso′ gyätä′to
Caddo 1. Ha′yo tă′ia’ ă′ă′
sections.text:
Nä′nisa′na, Nä′nisa′na,
Our father dwells above,
Our father dwells above,
Our mother dwells below,
Our mother dwells below.

sections.title: Caddo 2. Wû′nti ha′yano′ di′witi′a
sections.text:
Nä′nisa′na, nä′nisa′na,
All our people are going up,
All our people are going up,
Above to where the father dwells,
Above to where the father dwells,
Above to where our people live,
Above to where our people live.

sections.title: Caddo 3. Nû′na ĭ′tsiya′
sections.text:
I have come because I want to see them,
I have come because I want to see them,
The people, all my children,
The people, all my children.
He′yahe′eye! He′yahe′eye!

sections.title: Caddo 4. Na′tsiwa′ya
sections.text:
I am coming, I am coming,
The grandmother from on high, Wi′ahe′e′ye′,
The grandmother from on high, Wi′ahe′e′ye′,
Wi′ahe′e′ye′ye′yeahe′ye′,
Wi′ahe′e′ye′ye′yeahe′ye′!

sections.title: Caddo 5. Na′-iye′ ino′ ga′nio′sĭt
sections.text:
Wa′hiya′ne, wa′hiya′ne,
My sister above, she is painted,
My sister above, she is painted.
Wa′hiya′ne, wa′hiya′ne.

sections.title: Caddo 6. Na′a ha′yo ha′wano
sections.text:
Nä′nisa′na, nä′nisa′na,
Our father above (has) paint,
Our father above (has) paint.

sections.title: Caddo 7. Wû′nti ha′yano ka′ka′na′
sections.text:
Nä′nisa′na, nänisa′na,
All the people cried when I returned,
All the people cried when I returned,
Where the father dwells above,
Where the father dwells above.

sections.title: Caddo 8. Na′wi i′na
sections.text:
Nä′nisa′na, nä′nisa′na,
E′yahe′ya, e′yahe′ya, he′e′ye′!
E′yahe′ya, e′yahe′ya, he′e′ye′!
We have our mother below; we have our father above—He′yoi′ya, he′e′ye′!
We have our mother below; we have our father above—He′yoi′ya, he′e′ye′!

sections.title: Caddo 9. Ni′ ika′ na′a
sections.text:
There are our grandmother and our father above,
There are our grandmother and our father above;
There is our father above,
There is our father above.

sections.title: Caddo 10. Hi′na ha′natobi′na
sections.text:
The eagle feather headdress from above,
The eagle feather headdress from above,
From the eagle above, from the eagle above;
It is that feather we wear,
It is that feather we wear.

sections.title: Caddo 11. Na′ ăă′ o′wi′ta′
sections.text:
The father comes from above,
The father comes from above,
From the home of the Hai-nai above,
From the home of the Hai-nai above.

sections.title: Caddo 12. Na′ iwi′ o′wi′ta′
Caddo 13. A′nana′ hana′nito′
sections.text:
The feather has come back from above—He′e′ye′!
The feather has come back from above—He′e′ye′!
Is he doing it? Is he doing it?
The feather has returned from on high—He′e′ye′!
The feather has returned from on high—He′e′ye′!
Is he doing it? Is he doing it?

sections.title: Caddo 14. Na′ iwi′ ha′naa′
sections.text:
There is an eagle above,
There is an eagle above;
All the people are using it,
All the people are using it.
See! They use it,
See! They use it.

sections.title: Caddo 15. Wi′tŭ′ Ha′sini′
sections.text:
E′yehe′! Nä′nisa′na,
E′yehe′! Nä′nisa′na.
Come on, Caddo, we are all going up,
Come on, Caddo, we are all going up.
To the great village—He′e′ye′!
To the great village—He′e′ye′!
With our father above,
With our father above where he dwells on high—He′e′ye′!
Where our mother dwells—He′e′ye′!
Where our mother dwells—He′e′ye′!
